meta.blurb: Something huge is sinking ships in the dark, and nobody knows what it is. Professor Aronnax sails out to hunt it. The monster is a steel ship, and its captain, Nemo, says no guest may ever leave.
meta.bible: Professor Pierre Aronnax: a French naturalist and the narrator, curious, careful and honest. Conseil: Aronnax's loyal servant, calm and fond of sorting living things into groups. Ned Land: a Canadian harpooner, strong, blunt and always dreaming of escape. Captain Nemo: the mysterious captain of the Nautilus; learned, proud, sad and angry with the world; his name means no one in Latin. Nautilus: Nemo's electric submarine, with a library, a museum, an organ and big glass windows. Commander Farragut: the captain of the American ship Abraham Lincoln. Abraham Lincoln: the warship sent to hunt the monster. La Pérouse: a French explorer whose ships were lost near Vanikoro in 1788. Vanikoro: a Pacific island where his ships were wrecked. Crespo: an island in the Pacific where Nemo hunts underwater. Torres Strait: the dangerous strait between New Guinea and Australia. New Guinea: the large island north of Australia. Ceylon: the island where pearls are fished. Indian Ocean, Red Sea, Pacific, Atlantic, Mediterranean, Antarctic: oceans and seas on the way. Suez: the narrow land between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean. Arabian Tunnel: the secret passage under it. Vigo Bay: a Spanish bay with sunken treasure. Atlantis: a lost city on the sea floor. Sargasso Sea: a sea covered with floating weed. Cape Horn: the southern tip of South America. Gulf Stream: the warm Atlantic current. Lofoten: the Norwegian islands where the story ends. Maelström: a dangerous whirlpool off Norway. New York: where Aronnax is when the story starts. Voice and tone: wonder and adventure, told by Aronnax, with calm scientific detail and a growing mystery about Nemo; keep every sea fact true; deaths are stated plainly with no gore. Scotia: the steamship struck by the monster before the hunt begins. Brooklyn and New York: the harbour the Abraham Lincoln leaves. Ned Land: from Canada, ready with his harpoon and his gun. Nautilus facts: about seventy metres long, a double hull, a sharp steel ram, electricity from sodium taken from sea water, a small boat that fits in a hollow of the hull, a library of twelve thousand books and a salon museum with paintings, shells and pearls; the plates and spoons are marked with the letter N. Black Current: the warm Kuro Siwo current off Japan. Crespo Island: the forest where Nemo and his guests hunt in diving suits with air guns. La Pérouse: lost in 1788; his ships the Astrolabe and the Boussole were wrecked at Vanikoro; Dillon found relics in 1826; a French monument stands on the shore. Torres Strait: the Nautilus runs aground on a coral bank and is freed by the tide four days later. Papuans and islanders of New Guinea: they attack the Nautilus and are driven off by electric rails; no one is killed. Coral cemetery: where a crew member who died in an accident is buried. Gulf of Manaar: the pearl banks of Ceylon; Nemo's giant pearl, as big as a coconut, worth about ten million francs; Ned kills the shark that attacks an Indian pearl diver. Red Sea, Arabian Sea, Arabian Tunnel under the Isthmus of Suez, Greece, Gibraltar, Portugal, Spain, Africa, Arabia, Australia: the route to the Mediterranean and Atlantic. Vigo Bay: Spanish treasure ships sunk in 1702. Plato: told the story of Atlantis. Sargasso Sea: floating weed. Antarctic ice: the Nautilus goes under the ice bank and Nemo reaches the South Pole and plants a black flag with a golden N. Ice trap: the ice closes behind the ship; the air runs low; the crew cuts and melts a way out. Cape Horn and the Amazon: the way north. Giant squid: attack the Nautilus in the Atlantic; one crew member is lost; Nemo weeps. Gulf Stream: the warm current. Warship: the Nautilus rams and sinks a warship of the nation that took everything Nemo loved; he prays before a portrait of a woman and two children. Maelström and Lofoten Islands in Norway: the escape and the end. Deaths are stated plainly with no gore.

beats.scene: A long bright shape glows under dark waves beside a sailing ship
beats.summary: In 1866 sailors on many ships see a huge, glowing creature in the sea.

beats.scene: A steamship with a damaged side rolls in a grey sea
beats.summary: The steamship Scotia is struck by something unknown and is badly damaged.

beats.scene: Newspapers pile up on a café table while men argue loudly
beats.summary: Scientists and newspapers argue about whether the monster is a whale, a narwhal or a reef.

beats.scene: Professor Aronnax writes at a desk in a New York hotel room
beats.summary: Professor Aronnax, just back from an expedition, writes that the monster is a giant narwhal.

beats.scene: A messenger hands Aronnax a letter while his servant packs a trunk
beats.summary: The American navy invites Aronnax to join the hunt, and he and Conseil agree.

beats.scene: Aronnax and Conseil climb a gangway to the deck of a warship
beats.summary: Commander Farragut welcomes the two Frenchmen aboard the fast ship Abraham Lincoln.

beats.scene: A tall Canadian with a harpoon leans on the rail of the ship
beats.summary: Aronnax meets Ned Land, the best harpooner in the world, who does not believe in the monster.

beats.scene: Ned and Aronnax talk beside a chart of the oceans on the deck
beats.summary: Ned doubts that any animal could pierce a ship, but Aronnax argues that the narwhal could.

beats.scene: Crowds wave from the pier as a warship leaves New York harbour
beats.summary: The Abraham Lincoln leaves New York with crowds cheering and the whole country watching.

beats.scene: Sailors stare at a stormy headland as the ship rounds South America
beats.summary: The ship sails south round Cape Horn and enters the wide Pacific Ocean.

beats.scene: Sailors in oilskins scan a grey Pacific horizon with long telescopes
beats.summary: Weeks of searching in the Pacific find nothing, and the crew grows tired.

beats.scene: Ned Land laughs on the deck while sailors frown at the empty waves
beats.summary: Ned mocks the hunt, and sailors who once cheered now whisper that they want to go home.

beats.scene: Commander Farragut stands on the bridge with his hands behind his back
beats.summary: Farragut promises that if the monster does not appear in three days, the ship will turn for home.

beats.scene: A sailor in the rigging points at distant white water on a bright morning
beats.summary: False alarms with whales and drifting wood leave the crew angry and disappointed.

beats.scene: A long pale glow spreads over the black sea under a starry sky
beats.summary: On the last night a bright, glowing shape appears in the dark water.

beats.scene: The frigate heels over as her engines race after a glowing shape
beats.summary: The ship chases the creature at full speed, but it stays just out of reach.

beats.scene: Ned Land stands at the bow with a raised harpoon over the water
beats.summary: Ned Land throws his harpoon, and it hits the monster with a ring like metal on metal.

beats.scene: A dark smooth back slides away from the ship in the moonless night
beats.summary: The creature vanishes, and the ship waits in the dark for hours, with the guns ready.

beats.scene: Aronnax tumbles over the rail as water rushes up the ship's side
beats.summary: The monster strikes the frigate, and Aronnax is thrown into the sea.

beats.scene: Conseil holds up Aronnax in the dark water while Ned swims near
beats.summary: Conseil jumps in to save his master, and Ned Land joins them as the ship drifts away.

beats.scene: Three wet men climb onto a long, smooth, dark back in the sea
beats.summary: The three men climb onto a hard, smooth back, and Ned Land finds that it is made of metal.

beats.scene: Three men sit on a curved iron hull under a field of cold stars
beats.summary: They wait on the metal back through the night, and the creature carries them quietly across the sea.

beats.scene: A round iron hatch opens in the hull as hands reach for the men
beats.summary: At dawn the creature moves, and the men shout and pound on it until a hatch opens.

beats.scene: Masked men drag three struggling prisoners down a ladder into darkness
beats.summary: Strong men seize them and pull them inside, and the iron door closes behind them.

beats.scene: Three men feel their way around a pitch-dark iron cell
beats.summary: In a black cell the three men are hungry and frightened, and Ned Land is furious.

beats.scene: A silent steward lays a table with silver plates marked with an N
beats.summary: A steward brings them dry clothes and a meal, and every dish is marked with an N.

beats.scene: A tall man with a proud face stands in the doorway of the cell
beats.summary: A tall, calm man appears, speaks to them in French, and says that his name is Captain Nemo.

beats.scene: Nemo stands beside Aronnax with a large book in his hand
beats.summary: Nemo tells Aronnax that he has read his book about the sea, and that he respects it.

beats.scene: Nemo looks sternly at three tired men sitting in a bright room
beats.summary: Nemo says that they may never leave the ship, but that they will be treated as guests.

beats.scene: Ned Land clenches his fists while Nemo walks calmly out of the room
beats.summary: Ned rages at the captain, and Nemo leaves without anger, as if the matter were already settled.

beats.scene: A table set with shells, fish and sea plants beside a round window
beats.summary: Aronnax wakes to a meal in which everything, even the clothes, comes from the sea.

beats.scene: Tall shelves of books in many languages fill a long, bright room
beats.summary: Nemo shows Aronnax the library, with twelve thousand books, and tells him to use it freely.

beats.scene: A grand room with paintings on the walls and glass cases of shells
beats.summary: In the great salon, Aronnax finds famous paintings, statues and a museum of sea creatures.

beats.scene: Glass cases hold glowing pearls, pink shells and spiny sea stars
beats.summary: Nemo's collection of pearls and shells is richer than any museum on land.

beats.scene: Nemo sits at a great organ while soft music fills the room
beats.summary: Nemo plays the organ in the evening, and the music seems to ease his sadness.

beats.scene: Nemo leads Aronnax past tall machines humming in a clean white room
beats.summary: Nemo takes Aronnax to the engine room, where everything is worked by electricity.

beats.scene: Rows of glass jars and metal plates glow in a long engine room
beats.summary: The electricity comes from batteries which take their power from the sea water.

beats.scene: Nemo stands before a model of the ship with measuring tools on a table
beats.summary: Nemo gives the length and shape of the Nautilus and explains its double hull.

beats.scene: Water rushes into big tanks while the ship tips gently downward
beats.summary: The Nautilus fills her tanks and dives smoothly beneath the waves.

beats.scene: Aronnax and Conseil press close to a huge window with fish passing
beats.summary: The windows open on the deep, and Conseil names the fish that drift past.

beats.scene: Aronnax writes notes at a desk beside a window full of green water
beats.summary: Aronnax settles into his strange new life and fills notebooks with what he sees.

beats.scene: Ned Land marks days on his cabin wall with a nail
beats.summary: Ned Land counts the days of captivity and complains that he is losing his mind.

beats.scene: Nemo measures the sun's height with a bright brass instrument on deck
beats.summary: Nemo takes the sun's height at noon and says the ship's position, which no one else may know.

beats.scene: A warm dark current flows through a bright blue Pacific Ocean
beats.summary: The Nautilus follows the warm Black Current that flows northeast from the coast of Japan.

beats.scene: Aronnax stands on the deck of the ship under the stars at night
beats.summary: At night the ship rises, and Aronnax breathes the fresh air on the deck.

beats.scene: A small boat sits in a hollow in the side of the ship
beats.summary: Nemo shows Aronnax the small boat that fits snugly into the hull of the Nautilus.

beats.scene: Nemo looks across the empty ocean with the wind in his coat
beats.summary: Nemo tells Aronnax that on the sea no tyrant has power, and that he loves it as a free man.

beats.scene: Conseil shares a plate of fish with Ned Land in the dim cabin
beats.summary: Conseil says that the sea is a fine place to study, and Ned Land growls at his calm.

beats.scene: Aronnax reads a small note written in a neat hand on his table
beats.summary: A note from Nemo invites Aronnax and his friends to hunt in his forests of Crespo Island.

beats.scene: Ned Land holds a gun-shaped tube while Conseil laughs beside him
beats.summary: Ned and Conseil accept the invitation at once, for any change is welcome to them.

beats.scene: Men in rubber suits and copper helmets stand in a bright dressing room
beats.summary: The three guests put on heavy diving suits and take air tanks and lamps for the hunt.

beats.scene: Nemo and three guests wait in a small chamber as water fills it
beats.summary: The men step into a small chamber, which fills with sea water, and walk out into the ocean.

beats.scene: Four divers walk across pale sand under a green-blue sea
beats.summary: The divers walk across a wide sandy plain on the sea floor, and the light grows dim.

beats.scene: Aronnax points at a bright shell while Conseil raises his hands
beats.summary: Aronnax and Conseil cannot speak inside their helmets, so they point and make signs to each other.

beats.scene: Tall dark sea plants like trees rise in a thick forest under the water
beats.summary: The group enters a great forest of tall sea plants that sway in the current.

beats.scene: Nemo aims a strange gun at a swimming animal among the plants
beats.summary: Nemo and Ned hunt with guns that shoot air and electric bullets, and they bring down a sea otter.

beats.scene: A great sea bird falls into the water beside a diver
beats.summary: Ned shoots a large bird that was flying low over the waves above the forest.

beats.scene: Four divers lie on a soft bed of sand among the tall plants
beats.summary: Nemo signals for a rest, and the four men lie down in the silence of the forest.

beats.scene: A dim blue light shines between tall plants at the end of the day
beats.summary: As the sun sinks overhead, the hunters follow their lamps back across the plain.

beats.scene: The bright ship waits in the dark water with its windows lit
beats.summary: The hunters climb back into the Nautilus tired and happy, and Aronnax thinks about Nemo's secret world.

beats.scene: The Nautilus glides above coral islands in a vast blue Pacific
beats.summary: The Nautilus crosses thousands of leagues of the Pacific, passing many islands and coral reefs.

beats.scene: Conseil holds a notebook of fish while Aronnax points at the glass
beats.summary: Aronnax and Conseil fill their notebooks with new fish, and each day brings wonders.

beats.scene: Ned Land stares at the small boat in its hollow in the hull
beats.summary: Ned Land thinks about the small boat and about escape, but Aronnax asks him to be patient.

beats.scene: The Nautilus slips quietly below a wild stormy sea
beats.summary: A great storm rages above, but the Nautilus dives below it into calm water.

beats.scene: A French explorer's ships sail out of a port with white sails raised
beats.summary: Aronnax remembers La Pérouse, who sailed from France in 1785 and was lost in 1788.

beats.scene: Aronnax sees dark old anchors half-buried on the sea bed
beats.summary: At Vanikoro, the Nautilus passes the reef where the ships of La Pérouse were wrecked.

beats.scene: A rusty cannon and old iron lie in coral under green water
beats.summary: Through the window Aronnax sees an anchor, a cannon and other relics of the lost ships.

beats.scene: Nemo stands bareheaded at the window in the silent salon
beats.summary: Nemo, who has visited the place before, tells Aronnax that no man alive knows all of its secrets.

beats.scene: A small stone monument stands on a green shore above the reef
beats.summary: Aronnax learns that a French ship raised a monument to La Pérouse on the island years ago.

beats.scene: The Nautilus moves away from a lonely island at sunset
beats.summary: The Nautilus leaves Vanikoro and sails west towards the Torres Strait.

beats.scene: White waves break on dark rocks and coral in a narrow strait
beats.summary: The Nautilus enters the Torres Strait, a narrow channel full of reefs and shallow banks.

beats.scene: Nemo stands at the wheel in a small room with lights and dials
beats.summary: Nemo steers the ship himself through the dangerous channel, and the crew is silent.

beats.scene: The Nautilus leans on a bank of coral in a bright, shallow sea
beats.summary: In the night the Nautilus strikes a coral bank and sticks fast.

beats.scene: Nemo studies a chart of tides with his hands behind his back
beats.summary: Nemo is calm and says that the rising tide will lift the ship free in four days.

beats.scene: Ned Land smiles at the green shore of an island far away
beats.summary: Ned Land hopes that this is the chance to escape, and asks if he may go ashore.

beats.scene: A small boat with three men pulls away from the side of the ship
beats.summary: Nemo lets the three men go ashore in the small boat to hunt and gather food.

beats.scene: Ned Land kneels on a sandy beach and kisses the warm ground
beats.summary: The three men land on a wooded island near New Guinea, and Ned Land is overjoyed.

beats.scene: Conseil gathers coconuts from a palm tree on a sunny beach
beats.summary: On the island they find coconut palms and other fruit, and they eat their fill.

beats.scene: A fire burns on the sand while a pigeon cooks on a stick
beats.summary: Ned shoots wild pigeons, and the three friends cook and eat a fine meal on the beach.

beats.scene: Aronnax finds a broken branch and a footprint in the damp sand
beats.summary: Aronnax sees fresh footprints near the forest, and Nemo's warning about the people of the island returns.

beats.scene: Three travellers stand on a beach with baskets full of fruit
beats.summary: Aronnax warns his friends, and the three men gather their food and hurry towards the boat.

beats.scene: Dark figures with spears and slings run out of the trees
beats.summary: Islanders armed with spears and stones suddenly rush out of the forest, shouting.

beats.scene: A small boat pulls away from the beach as stones splash around it
beats.summary: The three men push off in the boat and row for their lives while stones fly over them.

beats.scene: Three out-of-breath men climb up the ladder onto the ship's back
beats.summary: They reach the Nautilus safely, and Nemo says that it was good that they returned in time.

beats.scene: Hundreds of canoes crowd around a long dark ship at sunrise
beats.summary: At dawn hundreds of islanders in canoes surround the Nautilus.

beats.scene: Islanders crawl across the ship's deck and pound on the round windows
beats.summary: The islanders swarm onto the deck and try to break the hatch, while the crew waits inside.

beats.scene: Islanders fall back from the iron rails with their arms in the air
beats.summary: Nemo sends a current through the ship's rails, and the islanders who touch it are thrown back.

beats.scene: Nemo stands calmly at the foot of the stairs with his arms crossed
beats.summary: Nemo says that he has not killed anyone, and that he only wishes to protect his ship.

beats.scene: Water rises around the Nautilus as the ship lifts free of the reef
beats.summary: At the high tide the Nautilus floats free of the coral and leaves the shallow water.

beats.scene: The island fades into the haze as the Nautilus dips below the water
beats.summary: The Nautilus slips away through the Torres Strait, and Ned Land sits silent in his cabin.

beats.scene: Aronnax lies awake in his dim cabin while the ship hums softly
beats.summary: The Nautilus leaves the strait behind, and Aronnax lies awake with thoughts of home.

beats.scene: Nemo stands at Aronnax's door with a worried face and a lamp
beats.summary: A crew member has been badly hurt in an accident, and Nemo asks Aronnax to help him.

beats.scene: A crew member lies in a bunk while Aronnax bends over him
beats.summary: Aronnax sees at once that the man's injury is too serious to cure, and the man dies in the night.

beats.scene: Divers in dark suits carry a wrapped body through a coral forest
beats.summary: Nemo carries the dead sailor to a coral cemetery under the sea.

beats.scene: A grave is dug in white sand between branches of pink coral
beats.summary: The crew buries their friend in a grave dug in the sea floor, and the divers kneel in silence.

beats.scene: Nemo stands with his back to Aronnax, looking at the grave
beats.summary: Nemo says that here his friend will sleep safe from the sharks, and Aronnax sees a gentler side of him.

beats.scene: Coral of many colours grows in a great ridge under a shining sea
beats.summary: The Nautilus passes the great coral reefs, and Conseil explains how tiny animals build them.

beats.scene: The Nautilus sails across a wide, empty sea under a blazing sun
beats.summary: The Nautilus enters the Indian Ocean, and Nemo asks Aronnax if he likes pearls.

beats.scene: Divers drop into the sea from a small boat in a calm bay
beats.summary: Nemo explains how the pearl fishers of Ceylon dive for oysters, and the danger of sharks.

beats.scene: Pearl oysters cover a rocky floor in the green light
beats.summary: The Nautilus settles on a bank of pearl oysters in the Gulf of Manaar, and Aronnax gazes at the bed.

beats.scene: Divers in heavy suits walk across a bed of grey pearl oysters
beats.summary: The next day Nemo, Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land walk among the oysters of the pearl banks.

beats.scene: Nemo holds an open oyster in his hands, showing a small pearl
beats.summary: Nemo explains how a pearl forms inside a shell, and he lets the oysters live.

beats.scene: A great stone cave opens in the sea floor beside a giant shell
beats.summary: Nemo leads his friends into a cave where a huge shell lies open on the rock.

beats.scene: A giant shell, wider than a table, holds a round white pearl
beats.summary: Inside the giant shell lies a pearl as large as a coconut, and its value could be ten million.

beats.scene: Nemo looks fondly at the shell while three friends stare in awe
beats.summary: Nemo says that he visits the pearl each year and leaves it to grow, without ever taking it.

beats.scene: A small dark diver sinks beside a sharp rock with a rope
beats.summary: On the next day an Indian pearl diver drops from a boat above to gather oysters.

beats.scene: A huge grey shadow rises from the deep behind the unaware diver
beats.summary: A great shark appears behind the diver, and its jaws open wide.

beats.scene: Nemo throws himself in front of the shark with a dagger in his fist
beats.summary: Nemo fights the shark with his knife, but the beast knocks him down.

beats.scene: Ned Land swims forward and drives his harpoon into a shark's side
beats.summary: Ned Land stabs the shark with his harpoon, and the beast dies, and the diver is saved.

beats.scene: An Indian diver sits on the sand holding a heavy bag of pearls
beats.summary: Nemo gives the diver a bag of pearls, and Aronnax sees his kindness to the poor.

beats.scene: The Nautilus glides north across a wide hot sea at sunrise
beats.summary: The Nautilus leaves Ceylon and sails north and west across the Arabian Sea.

beats.scene: A narrow sea lies between two dry, golden shores under a hot sun
beats.summary: The ship enters the Red Sea, and Aronnax studies its colour and its fish.

beats.scene: Aronnax and Nemo stand in front of a map of the Isthmus of Suez
beats.summary: Aronnax asks how the ship can reach the Mediterranean, for the Suez canal is not yet open.

beats.scene: The Nautilus dives into a dark underground passage lit by lamps
beats.summary: Nemo says that there is a secret tunnel, and the Nautilus dives into it at Suez.

beats.scene: Pale rock walls fly past the windows in a dark swift current
beats.summary: The Nautilus races through the Arabian Tunnel under the desert in a very short time.

beats.scene: The Nautilus rises into bright blue water as a new day begins
beats.summary: The ship comes up in the Mediterranean, and Aronnax sees the shores of the old world.

beats.scene: Ned Land whispers to Conseil near a window with a map of Greece
beats.summary: Ned and Conseil plan to escape in the Mediterranean, because Europe is close.

beats.scene: Green islands pass a window in the early light as the ship speeds on
beats.summary: The Nautilus passes the Greek islands so fast that Ned cannot find a chance to escape.

beats.scene: Aronnax gazes at a blue sea with old stone harbours on a far shore
beats.summary: Aronnax thinks about the history of the Mediterranean, but Nemo seems in a hurry.

beats.scene: A rocky headland rises over the narrow gate of the Strait of Gibraltar
beats.summary: In only two days the Nautilus crosses the whole Mediterranean and comes to the Strait of Gibraltar.

beats.scene: The Nautilus slips past a tall rock into the open grey Atlantic
beats.summary: The Nautilus passes Gibraltar and swims north along the coast of Portugal and Spain.

beats.scene: Burned old wooden ships lie in the dim light of a sunken bay
beats.summary: In Vigo Bay, Nemo shows Aronnax the wrecks of Spanish treasure ships sunk in 1702.

beats.scene: Crew members in diving suits carry iron chests and gold bars across the sand
beats.summary: Nemo's men gather gold and silver from the sunken ships and carry it to the Nautilus.

beats.scene: Nemo stands over a heap of gold coins with a thoughtful face
beats.summary: Nemo says that the treasure belongs to nobody, and that he will use it where it is needed.

beats.scene: A black mountain slope rises in the sea under a dim red glow
beats.summary: The Nautilus follows a slope to a plain that was once dry land, lit by a distant volcano.

beats.scene: Broken pillars and walls stand in a ruined city under the sea
beats.summary: Nemo and Aronnax walk among the ruins of a sunken city, in the red light of the volcano.

beats.scene: Nemo writes a name on a black rock with a piece of white stone
beats.summary: Nemo writes the word Atlantis on a rock, and Aronnax thinks of Plato's story.

beats.scene: Men with picks and lamps work in a dark tunnel in the sea floor
beats.summary: The Nautilus visits an undersea coal mine, where Nemo's men dig fuel for the batteries.

beats.scene: A wide sea is covered with floating weed under a pale blue sky
beats.summary: The Nautilus rises into the Sargasso Sea, a vast field of floating seaweed.

beats.scene: Small fish and crabs crawl among long yellow strands of weed
beats.summary: Aronnax studies the creatures that live in the weed, while the ship turns south.

beats.scene: The Nautilus sails across a wide cold sea under a grey sky
beats.summary: The Nautilus sails south through the Atlantic, and the air and the water grow colder.

beats.scene: A herd of big whales swims together while dark shapes dive at them
beats.summary: A pack of sperm whales attacks a herd of whales that have no teeth.

beats.scene: Nemo stands at the window and gives a short order to his crew
beats.summary: Nemo decides to help the herd, and the Nautilus dives to meet the attackers.

beats.scene: The Nautilus drives through red water among thrashing whales
beats.summary: The ship uses her ram like a sword, and the sea turns red as the whales die.

beats.scene: Ned Land cheers loudly in the salon while Aronnax looks away
beats.summary: Ned cheers the fight, and Aronnax is both thrilled and sad at what he has seen.

beats.scene: Tall white icebergs drift on a dark sea under a low sun
beats.summary: Further south the Nautilus meets the first icebergs, and the air is full of snow.

beats.scene: A high white cliff of ice stretches to the horizon over a grey sea
beats.summary: A huge wall of ice blocks the way, and the Nautilus floats before it.

beats.scene: Aronnax and Ned Land stand on the deck in the biting wind
beats.summary: Aronnax and Ned stand on the deck, and the cold stings their faces.

beats.scene: The Nautilus slides below a roof of ice into a pale blue world
beats.summary: The Nautilus dives and passes beneath the ice, where the sea is lit with a strange pale light.

beats.scene: The Nautilus surfaces in a calm sea ringed with ice and strange birds
beats.summary: The Nautilus rises in a calm sea beyond the ice, where penguins and seals watch from the floes.

beats.scene: The Nautilus glides between white walls of ice in a narrow channel
beats.summary: The Nautilus sails south through narrow channels of open water between great walls of ice.

beats.scene: A low grey shore of frozen rock appears through the mist
beats.summary: A cold, bare land appears ahead, and Nemo says that they have come near the end of the world.

beats.scene: A small boat is pulled up onto a stony beach under a pale sky
beats.summary: The small boat carries the men ashore, where penguins and seals gaze at them without fear.

beats.scene: Ned Land stands over a pile of birds in the snow with a smile
beats.summary: Ned Land hunts birds and seals for fresh food, and Aronnax gathers mosses and rocks.

beats.scene: Nemo sits alone on a high rock, looking south over a white land
beats.summary: Nemo tells Aronnax that he wishes to be the first man ever to stand at the southern pole.

beats.scene: Nemo holds a bright brass instrument up to a pale sun in the mist
beats.summary: The next day the mist lifts for a short time, and Nemo measures the height of the sun at noon.

B1B2: In 1866 captains on both sides of the ocean report a huge shape that glows at night. It swims faster than any whale, and nobody can say what it is.
The steamship Scotia is crossing the Atlantic when something strikes her side below the water. She stays afloat, but the hole is large, and the passengers never see what hit her.
Soon every newspaper in the world has its own idea about the monster. Some writers say it is a giant whale, while others believe it is a hidden reef or a sea serpent.

Professor Aronnax has just come home from a scientific journey across the American west. When a newspaper asks for his opinion, he writes that the monster must be a giant narwhal with a horn of unusual strength.
A letter arrives from the American navy, inviting Aronnax to help to hunt the monster. He says yes at once, and his servant Conseil, who follows him everywhere, packs the bags without a word.

The Abraham Lincoln is a fast steam frigate with a fine crew and the best guns in the navy. Her captain, Commander Farragut, welcomes the professor and promises him the comfortable cabin he has asked for.
Among the sailors is a tall Canadian called Ned Land, the best harpooner in the world. He is strong and proud, and he does not hide the fact that he thinks the monster is a story for children.
Ned says that no animal could pierce an iron ship, but Aronnax answers that the sea hides many creatures that science has never seen. The two men argue for an hour, and they end as friends.
On the day of departure thousands of people crowd the piers of New York, waving flags and calling out good wishes. The Abraham Lincoln leaves the harbour with her engines roaring and her flag flying.
For weeks the ship runs south through warm seas and then round the stormy tip of South America called Cape Horn. At last she reaches the Pacific Ocean, where the monster was last seen.
Week after week the Abraham Lincoln searches the Pacific without seeing so much as a shadow. The sailors stand at their posts all day, and their eyes grow tired and their tempers short.
Ned Land laughs at the whole expedition and says that the monster is a story for newspapers. The men who once cheered at the pier now whisper that they would like to go home.
At last Commander Farragut calls his crew together and makes a promise. If the monster does not show itself within three days, he says, the ship will turn round and sail for New York.
Twice a sailor shouts that he has found the creature, and twice the ship races towards a harmless whale. Each time the crew's hopes fall a little lower, and Ned laughs a little louder.
On the third night the sea is calm and the sky is full of stars. Suddenly a long, pale light appears on the water, and it seems to glow from somewhere far below.
Farragut orders full steam, and the frigate leaps forward with her engines roaring and her deck shaking. The creature stays ahead of her, as if it were playing with a slow animal.
Ned Land stands at the bow with his harpoon in his hand and waits until the shape is close. He throws with all his strength, but the point only rings against the monster's hide, as if on iron.
The glow suddenly goes out, and the sea around the ship is black and silent. The crew waits for hours with the guns ready, and nobody dares to speak.
Without any warning, a great force strikes the frigate from below and shakes her from end to end. Aronnax is thrown over the rail and falls deep into the cold water.
His heavy clothes drag him down, and he fights for breath in the dark. Conseil, who has jumped in after his master, holds him up, and Ned Land swims towards them as the ship drifts away.
The three men crawl out of the water and find a long, smooth back that is hard under their hands. Ned Land knocks on it, and he cries that the monster is made of iron.
They sit on the curved metal as the creature carries them quietly across the sea. Aronnax feels cold and weak, but he cannot stop thinking about what kind of machine could be so silent.
As dawn comes, the monster begins to move faster, and the three men almost fall into the water. They shout and strike the metal with their fists until a round door opens in the hull.
Strong hands, which belong to men wearing strange clothes, seize the prisoners and drag them down a ladder. The door closes with a heavy sound, and they are left in complete darkness.
The cell has no windows, no furniture and no light, and the three men do not know where they are. Ned Land is both hungry and furious, and he kicks the iron wall until his foot hurts.
At last a light comes on, and a silent steward brings dry clothes and a hot meal. Aronnax notices that every plate and spoon is marked with the letter N, and he wonders what it means.
The door opens, and a tall man with dark eyes and a proud face stands before them. He speaks perfect French and says calmly that he is Captain Nemo, the master of this ship.
Nemo explains that he has read Aronnax's book about the deep sea, and that he admires it. Aronnax is surprised and almost pleased, even though he is a prisoner.

The captain says that he has broken with the land and everything that belongs to it, and that his secret must be safe. For that reason none of the three may ever leave his ship, although he promises to treat them as guests.
Ned Land shouts that no man has the right to hold them against their will, and he uses some very rough words. Nemo listens without anger and leaves the room as if the matter were already settled.

The next morning the three men eat fish, shellfish and sea plants, and Aronnax finds the food delicious. He learns that his clothes are made of fine sea silk and that even the ship's paper comes from seaweed.
Nemo leads Aronnax into a long library with twelve thousand books in many languages. He says that the professor may read any of them, although there are no books about politics or money.
The great salon is as rich as a palace, with famous paintings on the walls and statues in the corners. In the middle stand glass cases full of shells and corals, each one marked with its name.
Aronnax cannot take his eyes off the pearls, which glow softly in their cases. Some are pink, some are black and some are as large as a bird's egg, and no museum could match them.
In the evening Nemo sits down at a large organ and plays for a long time. The music is slow and deep, and Aronnax feels that the captain is trying to forget something that hurts him.
Nemo takes Aronnax down to the engine room, which is clean and bright and almost silent. He says that the ship has no fire and no steam, because all its power comes from electricity.

The electricity is made in batteries that use sodium, which Nemo takes from the sea water around the ship. Because the sea will never run out, the Nautilus can sail for months without stopping for fuel.
The Nautilus is shaped like a long cigar and is about seventy metres long. It has two strong hulls, one inside the other, and a sharp ram at the front that can cut through the side of a ship.
When Nemo wants to dive, the crew fills big tanks with sea water, and the ship slowly grows heavy. Aronnax feels the floor tip gently, and soon the waves close over the windows of the salon.
Nemo touches a button, and two great steel shutters slide away from the glass. The three prisoners watch the fish of every shape drift past in the blue light, and Conseil names them one by one.
Aronnax slowly settles into his strange new life under the sea. He spends his days in the library and the salon, and he fills his notebooks with everything that passes the windows.
Ned Land counts the days of his captivity by making marks on the wall of his cabin with a nail. He complains that he is going mad, and he says that every hour on the ship is an hour lost.
At noon Nemo climbs to the top of the ship and measures the height of the sun with a brass instrument. He writes down the ship's position, but he never tells the professor where the Nautilus is.
For many days the ship follows a warm current that flows from the coast of Japan towards the northeast. The Japanese call it the Black Current, because its deep blue water looks almost dark.

One night the Nautilus rises, and Nemo lets Aronnax step out onto the narrow deck. The air is cool and sweet, the stars are very bright, and the professor stands there for a long time without speaking.

On Aronnax's table the next morning there lies a short note in a neat hand. It invites him and his two friends to hunt in the forests of Crespo Island, which belong to Captain Nemo.

To everyone's surprise, Nemo agrees and lets the three men take the small boat. He only warns them to be careful, because the people of that coast are said to be fierce.
The boat reaches the beach in less than an hour. Ned Land jumps onto the sand, kneels and kisses the warm ground, and he laughs like a child.

Nemo gives an order, and an electric current runs through the iron rails on the deck. Every islander who touches them cries out and falls back, and soon all of them are running to their canoes.

The Nautilus dives and slips out through the Torres Strait, leaving the island far behind. Ned Land sits in his cabin and does not speak, because his chance has gone.
The Nautilus leaves the Torres Strait behind and sails into open water. Aronnax cannot sleep, and he lies in his cabin thinking of his home and of everything he has lost.

Nemo turns to Aronnax and says that here his friend will sleep in peace, far from the sharks. Aronnax is moved, because he has not seen so much kindness in the captain before.
The Nautilus passes the long coral reefs, and Conseil tells Ned Land that tiny animals build such walls. Each one is no larger than a pin, and Ned Land listens with real interest for once.

The Nautilus passes the great rock of Gibraltar and swims out into the Atlantic. She turns north along the coast of Portugal, and Aronnax wonders where Nemo is taking them.

Crew members in diving suits walk across the sand and carry iron chests and bars of gold to the ship. Some of the chests have broken open, and old coins lie shining on the sea floor.

The Nautilus sails south through the Atlantic, and every day the air and the water grow colder. The three prisoners wear thick clothes, and the sun hangs low over a grey sea.

Nemo watches from the window and says that the sperm whales are the whales' worst enemies. He gives a short order, and the Nautilus dives to take the part of the herd.
The ship uses her ram like a sword and drives into the attackers, one after another. Within minutes the sea is red, and the few sperm whales that live swim away in fear.
Ned Land cheers loudly in the salon, because he has never seen a ship fight like a hunter. Aronnax is thrilled, but he is also sad, for he has never liked to see animals die.

Aronnax and Ned Land are allowed to stand on the deck for a few minutes in the wind. The cold stings their faces, and the silence is so deep that they can hear the ice crack far away.

The Nautilus sails south along narrow lanes of open water between huge walls of ice. The sun is very low, and the whole world looks as if it were made of glass.
One morning a bare, cold land appears through the mist ahead. Nemo says calmly that they have come near the end of the world, and he orders the small boat to be made ready.
Nemo, Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land take the boat to a stony beach, and they walk across the frozen ground. Penguins and seals look at them without fear, because they have never seen a man before.
Ned Land shoots some birds and seals for fresh food, and he drags them back to the boat with a broad smile. Aronnax and Conseil gather mosses and pieces of rock for their collection.
Nemo sits alone on a high rock, looking south across the white land. He tells Aronnax that he wishes to be the first man in the world to stand at the southern pole.
The next day the mist lifts for a short time, and Nemo measures the height of the sun at noon with his brass instrument. He writes a number in his book, and his face shines with a fierce joy.
On the top of the hill Nemo plants a black flag with a golden letter N. In a loud voice he says that he takes this place for himself and for his people.

As the sun touches the horizon, Nemo says goodbye to it, because the long polar night is about to begin. His voice shakes, and Aronnax is moved to see how deeply the captain loves the light he has left.
The four men row back through the drifting ice, and Aronnax thinks of the great explorers who failed to come here. In spite of himself, he is proud to have seen what they could not.
The Nautilus dives away from the white shore and turns north under the sea. Overhead the long night is beginning, and the ice is slowly growing thicker as the cold deepens.
In the middle of the night the Nautilus stops with a heavy shock, and Aronnax is thrown from his bed. When he runs to the window, he sees nothing but dark blue walls of ice on every side.
Nemo tells him quietly that the ice has shifted and closed behind the ship. The way out has gone, he says, and the Nautilus is now shut in a small lake under the frozen sea.
The captain looks at the gauge and says that there is air for only two days. Nobody speaks, and Ned Land turns pale beneath his tan.
Nemo calls his men together and orders them to cut a way out through the ice. They put on diving suits, take picks and axes, and walk out onto the ice with the lamps swinging.
Nemo also uses the engines to heat water, and he pumps it, boiling, against the walls of the ice. White steam fills the water around the ship, and the ice melts a little at a time.
As the hours pass, the air in the ship grows thick and warm, and the lamps burn low. Aronnax feels a heavy weight on his chest, and his head begins to ache.
Aronnax and Ned Land join the crew and swing picks at the ice for hours. Their arms hurt, but nobody stops, because they know that any man who rests may be the one who dies.
By the end of the second day the men have cut a deep channel under the ship. She begins to sink slowly into it, and the walls of the ice close in on both sides.
Nemo orders full power, and the Nautilus rushes forward and upward through the narrow place. She strikes the thin ice above her with her ram, and the roof breaks into pieces with a great noise.
Fresh air floods into the ship, and the three prisoners breathe it like men who have been dying of thirst. Nemo thanks his tired crew, and then he turns the ship north towards warmer seas.
The Nautilus sails north from the ice, and the cold slowly fades from the water. The three prisoners are tired but happy, and every day they feel a little more alive.
The ship passes Cape Horn, at the southern end of South America, where the wind blows hard. Aronnax thinks of the sailors who have died here, and he is glad to be below the waves.

Aronnax and Conseil spend long hours at the window, studying the fish of the Atlantic along the coast of South America. Conseil's notebook grows thicker every day, and he puts every new fish in its proper family.
In the quiet of the library Aronnax finds that he is beginning to respect Captain Nemo. It troubles him, because he knows that the man is also his jailer.
The Nautilus comes to the mouth of the Amazon, where the sea is full of fresh water for many miles. Aronnax tastes it and is amazed that a river can push so far into the ocean.
A great shoal of silver fish rushes past the windows, and then a school of dolphins comes to play around the ship. Conseil laughs and claps his hands like a child.
One evening Aronnax asks Nemo why he has left the world of men. Nemo smiles sadly and says that he will tell the professor everything one day, but he does not say when.
At night the ship rises, and Aronnax steps out on the deck under a sky full of stars. He finds the stars of the northern sky, and he feels that he is nearly home.
Ned Land speaks quietly to Aronnax while Conseil keeps watch at the door. He says that the time to escape is coming, and Aronnax promises that he will think about it.
The Nautilus turns towards the north and west, and Aronnax sees that the course points at North America. Ned Land watches the charts all day, and his hope begins to grow again.
One afternoon a dark shape appears at a window of the salon, and the Nautilus stops in the open Atlantic. The engines fall silent, and Aronnax stares into the dim water.
A giant squid presses against the glass, with eight long arms, huge round eyes and a hard beak like a parrot's. Aronnax estimates that its body is longer than a boat, and Conseil goes pale.
Nemo orders the ship to rise to the surface and sends his men up the stairs with axes. Ned Land takes a harpoon and follows them, and Aronnax and Conseil go with him.
When the hatch is opened, a long grey arm pushes through the narrow gap and feels around the stairs. A crew member strikes it with an axe, and the arm falls twitching to the floor.
On the deck the crew fights the squid, which are rising from the water on every side. A black cloud of ink spreads over the sea, and the waves are full of waving arms.
Suddenly a huge arm seizes a crew member and lifts him high into the air. The man cries out for help, and the squid carries him away over the sea before anyone can save him.
Another arm closes around Ned Land and begins to crush him. He fights it with his harpoon until Conseil and Nemo cut him free with their axes, and he falls on the deck, gasping.
At last the surviving squid slip back into the water and vanish. The sea is calm again, and the deck is slippery with ink and the blood of the monsters.
Nemo stands alone at the broken rail and looks at the place where his man was taken. Aronnax sees tears run down the captain's face, and he can say nothing.
Nemo shuts himself in his cabin for days, and the whole crew moves through the ship in silence. Aronnax feels pity for the man, and he begins to understand how heavy his sorrows are.
The Nautilus follows the Gulf Stream, a warm river that flows through the cold Atlantic. Aronnax explains that it carries as much water as many rivers together, and he has never seen such a blue.
Ned Land tells Aronnax that the escape must be made when the ship is close to a coast. He has marked a place on the chart, and he asks the professor to be ready on the first calm night.
One morning a thick fog covers the sea, and the Nautilus rises to the surface. Aronnax peers out from the deck and sees the dim shapes of ships far away in the mist.
A big warship with tall masts and black guns comes out of the fog and begins to follow the Nautilus. Aronnax cannot tell her flag, and Nemo says nothing at all.
Nemo's face turns hard and cold, as Aronnax has never seen it. He sends his three guests to their cabins and locks the doors, and he stays at the window alone.
The warship fires at the Nautilus, and Aronnax hears the shot hit the water nearby. Nemo orders the ship to dive and to turn around, so that she faces the enemy.
The Nautilus drives forward under the water, and she strikes the warship with her ram. The old ship cracks open, and the sea rushes in as she begins to sink.
Aronnax is allowed to the window, and he sees the warship go down with all her men. He turns away in horror, and he cannot understand how Nemo can do such a thing.
Aronnax goes to Nemo's cabin and finds him on his knees before a small portrait of a woman and two children. Nemo whispers a prayer and cries out in a broken voice that it is enough.
Nemo turns and says that the nation of the ship has taken everything that he ever loved. Aronnax cannot forgive what he has seen, and he decides that he will leave the Nautilus, whatever the cost.
For days afterwards Nemo hardly speaks, and he is hardly seen. The Nautilus drifts north through storms, like a ship that has lost its way, and the crew goes about its work in silence.
Aronnax tells Ned and Conseil in a low voice that he has decided to escape. Ned is overjoyed, and he says that he has been waiting for this moment since the first day.
The Nautilus nears the coast of Norway, and the sea grows rough. A great storm rises around her, and the waves beat at her sides like fists, although the ship feels no fear.
Late at night the three friends creep through the dark passages to the small boat. Ned Land begins to loosen the bolts that hold it, and Conseil keeps watch at the door.

Suddenly a bell rings in the ship, and Aronnax hears the crew cry out one word in a language that he cannot understand. He feels the whole ship begin to turn, and he knows that something is terribly wrong.
The Nautilus has been caught by the Maelström, a huge and terrible whirlpool off the coast of Norway. The bolts give way, and the small boat tears free and spins round the edge of the whirlpool.
The boat is thrown about like a leaf, and the foam hisses all around it. Aronnax is thrown against the side, and he loses his senses as the world turns to black.
When Aronnax wakes, he is lying in a bed in a fisherman's small hut on the Lofoten Islands. Ned Land and Conseil are safe beside him, and the fishermen are kind and ask no questions.
Aronnax sits down at a table by the window and begins to write the story of the voyage. He does not know what has happened to Captain Nemo, and he is not sure that he ever will.
Aronnax finishes by saying that he hopes Nemo has found peace and that his hatred has gone. He wishes that the Nautilus is still sailing, and that the sea still shelters its captain.
